population-and-age.change: En dashes in age ranges; source values unchanged.

regional-households.change: Santa Rosa panel only; Los Lunas is discussed in Chapter 7.

events.text: The move from Cabra to Cuervo was complete by year end.
A school was being built; lumber stock was withdrawn; the depot platform was improved.
A teacher left. Ninth-grade instruction was interrupted and a replacement was proposed.
Katharine A. Hicks withdrew financial support and argued for publication at Santa Rosa.
events.reference: Chapter 4, note 13; Chapter 7, note 7. Clipper, December 1, 1922.

events.text: Rittenhouse recorded gas and groceries, but no cafe, garage or tourist accommodation.
events.reference: Chapter 6, note 6. Rittenhouse, A Guide Book to Highway 66 (1946), pp.73-74.

events.text: The highway southwest of Cuervo moved to a new course.
The merchant still operated. Advertised local passenger stops disappeared between April and October.
events.reference: Chapter 3, note 17; Chapter 6, note 12. Grubbs p.115; April 27 and October 26 timetables.

events.text: The documented nearby I-40 project was built, decades after the first recorded withdrawals.
events.reference: Chapter 6, note 21. NTSB report, project near mileposts 282.7-290.7.

events.text: Cuervo was listed without an agent. Its billing was assigned to Tucumcari, as was Santa Rosa's.
events.reference: Chapter 6, note 17. Rock Island Station Book, December 15, C15 / PDF p.67.

events.text: A funeral Mass was announced at the Cuervo church; the notice also described restoration work.
events.reference: Chapter 8, note 7. Dorothy Chavez obituary, March 2017.

events.text: A 2020 ranch purchase outside Cuervo was reported in 2026. The operation became a conservation-award finalist that year.
events.reference: Chapter 8, notes 1-2. January 2026 interview; July 2026 Leopold Conservation Award finalist announcement.

events: Dec 1974 / No agent; billing at Tucumcari
